# Performance: pass-with-notes

Subject: pr:310. Round 1. Exact head: 92787c46d0fef581b36fe93e426d90b671f502a1.

No performance blocker in the A1 idle-poll cut. This is source/CI approval with live BEFORE evidence, not a deployed AFTER result. No bounce, dependency installation, competing receiver, local build, or product-worktree edit was performed.

## Cost verified from code

`crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs:1992-2010,2270-2299` creates one live subscription before the first claim and replaces the native 500 ms tick with the next due-time timer, capped at 15 s, plus the unchanged 55 s answer deadline. Both native idle and during-turn waits use the due-time read. Every matching seat event permits another pass; unrelated events do not.

With no matching event or timed work, a 55 s native request makes four passes, at approximately 0, 15, 30 and 45 s. The deadline branch returns without a final claim pass. Across 76 continuously waiting seats, that is approximately 5.53 passes/s versus 152/s before; the PR's approximate five passes/7 per second is conservative. Active work and delayed/leased rows add passes, so this is not an unconditional fleet ceiling.

For a truly empty SQLite inbox, each pass costs six existing statements: two registry reads, each with its schema check, plus the queue schema check and live-kind preflight. `next_claimable_in` adds TWO statements, its `PRAGMA user_version` and the indexed MIN query (`crates/store/src/queue.rs:95-129,868-889`; `registry.rs:414-422`; `migrate.rs:242-245`). Empty-loop SQL therefore falls from approximately 912 to 44 statements/s at 76 waiters, excluding fixed request admission and event-driven work. The due query uses `jobs_claimable(state,kind,id)` but visits matching pending/running rows; it is not O(1) in that seat's live backlog. Terminal history and other seats' kinds are excluded.

No new process launch or launch site. Timers, subscription filtering and the added SQL run in-process.

## Live BEFORE receipts

Daemon PID 22838, commit 653f90ef96, same process-start identity at both edges. November 21, 2026, 04:55:09.077-04:56:09.108 UTC:

| Measure | Receipt |
|---|---|
| Interval | ping 60.030824 s; ps 60.027686 s |
| Inbox completions | 141 success, 0 refusal; ok 10710 -> 10851 |
| Inbox active | 1191025956 -> 1200180721 us; delta 9154765 us |
| Active/completion; active/second | 64.927 ms; 152.501 ms/s |
| Daemon cumulative CPU | 1860.70 -> 1875.70 s; 15.00 s, 24.988% of one core |
| RSS | 116576 -> 121840 KiB; no leak inference from this short change |
| Exact daemon launches | 14, 0.2332/s |

Commands: `pij-rs --json ping`, twice with a 60 s sleep; `/bin/ps -p 22838 -o time=,rss=,lstart=,comm=`, at both edges. Launch deltas reconcile: ddocs.community 2, git.community 7, ps.tmux-harness-process-tree 2, and tmux.new-window/pipe-pane attach/set-options tap owner 1 each.

Separate command `just spawn-rate --seconds 20 --json`: 388.7 total launches/s; 365.7 sampled/s, a lower bound. No daemon child was observed in THAT separate window; that does not contradict the exact 14 launches in the CPU window. The busy machine sampler did not overlap the CPU window.

This was not a quiet isolated control: it also completed one spawn, two adopts, one output, 16 sends and 626 whoami calls. Do not substitute its 25% CPU for the PR's quieter 16-20% controls or attribute all CPU to inbox.

## Broadcast fan-out

`events/mod.rs:132-149,261-280,445-479` broadcasts every event to every receiver, cloning `Event` before kind/seat filtering. With W waiters and E events/s, receive/filter work scales as W*E, and payload-copy work as W*event bytes/s. The subscription is request-local and drops with the request; this patch adds no per-event subscription or process.

A separate read-only, bounded live-spine window on the same PID/commit, 04:58:27.058-04:58:47.074 UTC, observed seq 4691617 -> 4691628: 11 events in 20.015596 s, 0.5496/s, with 2012 payload bytes. At 76 waiters that predicts approximately 41.77 event receives/s and 7.64 KB/s of payload copying, excluding Event/String overhead. These are estimates from durable events, not measured subscriber polls or CPU. Four events were delivery.outcome, and only their target waiters perform a full claim pass.

Fan-out can therefore dominate native-wait wake/receive COUNT after removing the tick, but this small sample does not establish CPU dominance. It is inherited, not newly introduced. Importantly, `HeldSpan` encloses `subscription.next()`, so filter/clone processing inside the wait is excluded from inbox `active_us`; use actual daemon CPU and event-rate evidence, not the route reduction alone.

## Proof and AFTER obligation

`just pr-freeze 310`: FINAL at this exact head, all five CI checks passed. Verified successful Rust run 44867815618, job 136735344617, artifact 14691978813 selected from that job's upload log: all 12 focused tests passed, including the seven next-claimable store tests, four real-store wake/identity tests, and the six-recipient-read bound over 20 s for both wait modes. The reported three mutants were not independently rerun in this read-only performance review.

Local `harness boot --json` returned ready=false because node_modules is absent. `harness checks --quick --json` exited 1: missing tsx/TS dependencies prevented several sensors, and the ambient Biome could not parse the repository's Biome 2 config. Pij-skill, copilot-native and copilot-sdk passed; Rust/route-inventory/smoke were skipped by --quick. These are not green local gates. Exact-head CI supplies the dependency-backed proof under C25; dependencies were not installed or linked.

After the prime's bounce, wait at least one complete 55 s request lifetime so pre-bounce requests cannot contaminate the endpoint delta. Record the new PID/commit and repeat matched 60-120 s ping/ps windows plus a separate 20 s spawn-rate window. Show substantially lower inbox active/completion and active/second; the source expectation is an approximately twentyfold empty-loop statement reduction, not a guaranteed wall-time ratio. Show lower daemon CPU on a comparable cohort/activity mix, with RSS and exact per-site launch deltas retained.

Pass expectation: four undisturbed empty passes per 55 s request, plus matching-event/timed-work passes; six recipient reads over 20 s including admission. Ping reports COMPLETIONS, not inner passes. Until live pass instrumentation exists, explicitly retain the pass bound as source/CI proof rather than claim it was measured after deployment. Record concurrent event throughput before attributing residual CPU to fan-out.

Harness magicWand: a read-only cost-window command that pairs route/CPU/spawn deltas and exposes inner-pass and subscriber-receive counters, keeping broadcast CPU distinct from HeldSpan-subtracted wall time.
